newsitem.title: USA: Swiss Ombudsman on bank accounts a flop -- Jewish group.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Ombudsman on bank accounts a flop -- Jewish group.

text.p: A Jewish group called a Swiss Ombudsman's effort to find the assets of Holocaust victims a "cruel farce" on Monday, saying not a single penny has been returned to survivors or their relatives after a year-long probe.

"After 2,000 inquiries and 1,000 formal claims, the Swiss Ombudsman has returned not a cent. He has rejected every claimant for a year. This is a cruel farce perpetuated on Holocaust survivors by the Swiss banking industry," World Jewish Congress vice president Kalman Sultanik said.
In a statement, Sultanik said that claimants paid up to 300 Swiss francs a search and had to fill out detailed forms in which they were even asked to produce death certificates.

The issue of which assets of Holocaust victims remain in Swiss banks has been a controversial one, with Jewish groups saying they believe that many millions of dollars are unaccounted for and that Swiss banks are stonewalling efforts to retrieve them.
Sultanik said the Ombudsman was appointed to counter the withering criticism the Swiss banking industry had received, but had failed to improve the situation.
